newsitem.title: INDIA: Death toll climbs to 46 in south Indian rains.
newsitem.headline: Death toll climbs to 46 in south Indian rains.

text.p: The death toll from torrential rains and flash floods in the southern Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh has risen to 46 with thousands left homeless in the last five days, officials said.

Officials in Andhra Pradesh, where at least 36 people have died, said life had come to a standstill in many parts of the state as thousands of mud houses collapsed and crops were destroyed in the steady downpour.
The incessant rains brought dangerous flooding, washed out roads, destroyed railway tracks, closed major bridges and uprooted trees.

Chandrababu Naidu, chief minister of Andhra Pradesh, said rescue operations were being carried out by army helicopters with people airlifted from the flood-affected coastal areas of Cuddapah and Prakasam districts.
"The majority of deaths in the monsoon season occurred predominantly due to the collapse of houses and electrocution caused by rains and floods," said an Agriculture Ministry expert.
Officials in Tamil Nadu's capital city Madras said non-stop rain for two hours on Friday dumped more than five inches (14 cm) of water in the city and damaged 45,000 huts in low-lying coastal areas.
They said rainstorms had severed telecommunication links and left affected areas virtually cut off from the outside world.
Officials organising relief operations in Andhra Pradesh said the army and air force had helped evacuate at least 30,000 people from affected areas.
The downpour, caused by a low pressure area in the Bay of Bengal, marked the begining of the northeast monsoon rains, officials said.
Losses in land and property are still being estimated.
